Start the long-lived MCP stdio server; newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdin/stdout, no Content-Length headers.
4-line shim that requires ../dist/mcp-server.js.
initialize answers {protocolVersion:"2024-11-05",capabilities:{tools:{}},serverInfo:{name:"cool-workflow",version:CURRENT_COOL_WORKFLOW_VERSION}}.
tools/list answers {tools:[196 definitions]} in source order, cw_list first, cw_history last; must equal toolDefinitions() exactly.
tools/call answers {content:[{type:"text",text:JSON.stringify(result,null,2)}]} — the core result as a 2-space pretty JSON string.
Every server message is JSON.stringify(message)+"\n" on stdout; input lines are split on \n, trimmed, empty lines skipped.
Broken JSON line answers {code:-32700,message:"Parse error: <JSON.parse message>"} with id null, even when the line held an id.
Unconsumed stdin buffer over MAX_LINE_BYTES=16*1024*1024 with no newline is dropped and answered with code -32700 message "Parse error: request line exceeds 16777216 bytes", id null.
Valid JSON that is not an object (number/string/array/null) answers {code:-32600,message:"Invalid Request: not a JSON-RPC object"} with id null.
Unknown method with an id key (null counts) answers {code:-32601,message:"Unknown method: <method>"}; an id-less unknown method gets no answer at all.
Any error thrown by tool name/argument checks or the core answers {code:-32000,message:<error message>} with the request id.
tools/call with params.name missing, empty, or spaces-only throws "MCP tools/call missing required field: name" (-32000).
A tool name not in the dispatch switch throws "Unknown tool: <name>" (-32000).
Non-object arguments throw "MCP tool <name> arguments must be an object."; null/absent arguments become {}.

Required-argument groups come from registry data (McpBinding.requiredArgs); group "a|b" needs one key that is not undefined, null, or ""; failure throws "MCP tool <name> missing required argument: a or b".

A non-empty args.cwd is path.resolve-d, must be a directory (else "MCP cwd is not a directory: <path>"), is written back into a copy of args, and re-bases the runner via withBaseDir(cwd); Scheduler/RoutineTriggerBridge use cwd||process.cwd().

Dispatch is an explicit switch by design; descriptor.entry does not reliably name the called function (cw_app_run entry=validateApp calls appRun; cw_commit entry=commit calls commitEnvelope) — a generic dispatcher would false-green.
Every tool inputSchema is {type:"object",properties,additionalProperties:true}; unknown extra keys pass through to the core.

Property values are string/number/boolean/object(additionalProperties:true)/array(items:{}) helpers; two hand-written exceptions: cw_commit.allowUnverifiedCheckpoint (plain boolean) and cw_routine_fire.payload (object with NO additionalProperties key).
cw_workbench_serve forces once:true and only returns the serve descriptor identical to `cw workbench serve --json`; it never starts the blocking localhost host (declared divergence).
cw_ledger_review upper-cases verdict and refuses anything but APPROVED/REJECTED with error 'verdict must be "approved" or "rejected".'.
cw_ledger_list with dirs array of 2+ union-verifies mirrors (unionLedgerEntries); else listLedgerEntries(dirs[0] || dir).
cw_topology_show with runId AND (topologyRunId or id) shows a topology run; else shows the official topology named by topologyId/id.
cw_routine_fire fires with args.payload || args — with no payload key the whole args bag is the event payload.
CAPABILITY_REGISTRY (209 capabilities, 196 MCP tools, 13 cli-only, 0 mcp-only) is the one declared source both surfaces are gated against; dedupe by capability id, last declaration wins.
buildParityReport fails closed on: tool/token on one surface only, live-but-undeclared tools/tokens, help-token gaps, reasonless exceptions, probe misclassification, registry lint.

For every non-opted-out both-surface capability, `cw <cmd> --json` must byte-equal the cw_<tool> result after neutralizing ISO timestamps (and for scenarios: workspace roots, run/snapshot/replay/dispatch ids, durationMs, sha256/hex64).
74 payload probes: 7 global, 24 run-scoped, 43 scenario; every payload-identical capability must be classified exactly once or deferred with a reason, else the gate fails.
A capability escapes the payload probe only with BOTH payloadIdentical:false AND a non-empty reason; a bare payloadIdentical:false stays probed (fail closed).

Exactly 12 declared payload-divergent (projected) capabilities: commit, backend.agent.config.set, run.drive.step, gc.run, clones.gc, orphans.gc, workbench.serve, ledger.propose, ledger.review, ledger.verify, ledger.apply, ledger.list.
Exactly 13 declared cli-only capabilities: help, version, update, fix, info, search, man, doctor, loop, schedule.daemon, quickstart, demo.tamper, demo.bundle — each with a recorded reason.
The live gate runs real cw help and checks every declared CLI path through the dispatcher lookup; it does not use a token list made from the registry as proof of the same registry.
